name: Matthew
title: The Tax Collector Who Became an Apostle
summary: Matthew, also called Levi, was a tax collector in Capernaum before Jesus called him. Tax collectors were despised as sinners and collaborators with the Romans. Jesus called him from his tax booth, and Matthew left everything to follow Him. He is traditionally regarded as the author of the Gospel of Matthew.

keyEvents.title: The Call at the Tax Booth
keyEvents.description: Jesus saw Matthew sitting at the tax booth and said, 'Follow me!' Matthew got up and followed Him.

keyEvents.title: The Meal with Tax Collectors
keyEvents.description: Matthew hosted a great feast for Jesus with many tax collectors and sinners. The Pharisees criticized this.

keyEvents.title: Jesus Defends Sinners
keyEvents.description: When the Pharisees criticized Jesus for eating with tax collectors, He answered, 'I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.'

keyEvents.title: One of the Twelve
keyEvents.description: Matthew was chosen as one of Jesus' twelve apostles; the list of the twelve names him as 'Matthew the tax collector.'

keyEvents.title: The Gospel's Author
keyEvents.description: Tradition attributes the first gospel to Matthew, written especially for Jewish readers with many OT quotations.
